basic_identification.full_title: Sports Footwear — Part 1: General Purpose (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Footwear (approved by the Chemical Division Council and finalized by the Footwear Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard prescribes requirements, methods of sampling, and test procedures for general-purpose sports footwear (such as walking, fitness, exercising, and light sports activities). It applies to footwear designed to minimize wear fatigue and maximize durability across varied general athletic environments, excluding high-performance specialized athletic footwear.

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: First Revision, June 2023 (incorporating Amendment No. 1, January 2024 and Amendment No. 2, October 2025)

revision_history.edition: First Revision (split into three parts based on uses)

amendment_slips.description: Inserts Clause 3.4 defining 'Insock' as a removable or non-removable footwear component covering all or part of the insole. Substitutes Clause 4.2 to classify general-purpose sports footwear into two main usage categories: For Kids (standard English sizes per IS 1638) and For Adults (all other sizes per IS 1638, further divided into Type 1 and Type 2). Completely replaces Table 1 with updated whole footwear physical requirements.

Amends Table 1, Sl No. (x), col (3), col (4), col (5) to substitute 'Category 1 and Category 2' for 'Category I and Category II'. Substitutes Clause C-3.1 to specify the load cell capacity of the tensile testing machine (<= 50 kg with jaw separation speed of 100 ± 10 mm/min and least count of 0.01 kg). Corrects a typographical error in Clause C-6, substituting 'interface' for 'infaiterface'. Completely replaces G-1.6 and G-2.1.4 equations to standardize the percentage of compression set calculations.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Footwear made from Leather and other Materials (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all general-purpose sports footwear manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Micro and small units (MSEs) are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to sports shoes.

requirements.detail: Every sports shoe must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on a secure label or embossed permanently, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

Footwear size categories are split into two groups based on age: a) Kids: Standard English sizes for children per IS 1638; b) Adults: Standard English sizes above kids' ranges, further divided into Type 1 and Type 2.
The insock, if used, cannot be removed without damaging the footwear. This is a mandatory safety requirement for Kids, Adults (Type 1), and Adults (Type 2).
To maintain ergonomic gait mechanics during fitness and walking, the minimum toe spring height must be 2 mm for all categories (Kids, Adults Type 1, and Adults Type 2).
The heel/seat region must demonstrate high impact cushioning. The test is performed using a standard compression punch per IS 15298 (Part 1) to apply forces up to 6 000 N.

Outsoles must resist wear: a) Outsole abrasion is tested separately for cellular and solid outsoles; b) PU outsoles must pass a hydrolysis test to ensure they do not crumble in wet climates; c) Complete shoe flexing is evaluated per IS 8085 (Part 16) / ISO 24266 Method A.
Tensile testing machines used for checking bond strength must use a load cell with a capacity of <= 50 kg, jaw separation speed of 100 ± 10 mm/min, and a high-precision least count of 0.01 kg.

The exact mathematical compression set percentage must be calculated and expressed using the formula: 
Percent compression set = (t0 - ti) x 100 / t0, where t0 is initial thickness and ti is final thickness after recovery.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15844 (Part 1) : 2023 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification establishing physical, mechanical, and safety requirements for general-purpose sports footwear (such as fitness, exercise, and walking shoes). Under the mandatory national Footwear QCO, all such sports footwear supplied to the Indian market must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify structural and chemical safety. It categorises shoes into Kids and Adults (Type 1 and Type 2) size classes, requiring non-removable insocks and a minimum toe spring height of 2 mm. It enforces high upper-to-sole bond strength (up to 2.5 N/mm for adult Type 1), flexing durability, and complete chemical compliance (including limits on carcinogenic dyes, Azo amines, and heavy metals) per IS 17011. Amendment No. 2 (October 2025) refines tensile machine calibration tolerances and standardizes the mathematical formula used to calculate heel compression sets.
